results.query: A contractor proposed a steel stake vertical spacing of 15 ft [4.6 m] at the centre of each enclosure for silt fence installation per Plan 606-4B. Is this compliant with the required spacing in the standard plan?

According to Plan 203-2A grading notes, the contractor proposes to scarify the fill-section surface to a depth of only 2 inches [50 mm]. Verify whether this scarification depth is compliant with the required specification.

The contractor's submission for Plan 511-1A proposes a V-mesh end strip height of 3'-6" [1.07 m] in the EXPANDED VIEW. Is this dimension consistent with the required end strip height shown on the standard plan?

For Plan 203-2A, the contractor plans a Moisture Density Control (MDC) depth of 5 feet [1.5 m] below the ditch bottom, citing Note H. Verify whether this depth meets the maximum specified in the grading notes.

In the stake spacing table of Plan 511-1A, the contractor proposes a 'DOWN' stake spacing of 8.0 feet [2.4 m] for a 1V:3H slope configuration. Does this match the value required in the STAKE SPACING TABLE?
The proposed guardrail post spacing in Plan 606-7C installation is 12 ft [3.66 m]. Verify whether this exceeds the maximum allowable post spacing specified by the standard.

For Plan 202-1 mailbox installation, the proposed clearance between the mailbox face and the edge of the travelled way is 2 feet [0.6 m]. Verify compliance with the minimum offset requirement in the standard.

The contour ditch cross section proposed for a Plan 203-2A application has a depth of 6 inches [150 mm] and a bottom width of 6 inches [150 mm]. Verify whether these dimensions satisfy the minimum cross-section requirements on the grading notes.
A contractor's gabion basket installation per Plan 511-1A omits the geotextile fabric underlayment described in the plan notes. Is the installation compliant with Plan 511-1A?
For Plan 203-2A, the contractor proposes fill compaction without performing the moisture density control procedure referenced in the grading notes. Is this practice compliant?
The contractor installs silt fencing per Plan 606-4B but does not include the wire ties specified for the enclosure in the plan notes. Verify whether omitting the wire ties is compliant.
For guardrail end-treatment installation per Plan 606-7C, the contractor skips the crash-attenuator anchoring detail described in the plan's installation notes. Verify compliance.
For Plan 203-2A contour ditch construction, the contractor installs the ditch on the downslope side of the right-of-way instead of following the location rule in Grading Note D. Is this compliant?
A drainage pipe installation under Plan 511-1A omits the bedding gravel layer referenced in the installation notes and places the pipe directly on compacted subgrade. Is this compliant?

For Plan 202-1, the contractor installs a mailbox without attaching the breakaway support detail referenced in the plan notes. Verify whether the installation is compliant with the breakaway requirement.
For Plan 203-2A fill section construction, the contractor skips scarification of the existing ground surface described in the grading notes before placing fill. Is this compliant?

In Plan 511-1A EXPANDED VIEW, the contractor used steel stakes in place of wire ties at the centre of each enclosure where the plus (+) symbols are shown. Is this substitution compliant with the symbol convention on the plan?

For a gabion basket installation following Plan 511-1A page 2, the contractor omitted the internal diaphragms and used a single-cell construction. Is this compliant with the standard plan's internal component requirement?

A Plan 605-1 underdrain installation uses the drainage fabric as a horizontal separator layer above the gravel, instead of lining the trench bottom and vertical sides as depicted in the plan. Is this compliant?
For Plan 606-4B silt fence installation, the contractor uses wooden stakes in place of the steel stakes shown in the plan symbol legend. Is this substitution compliant?

A Plan 606-7C guardrail end treatment uses a concrete end anchor in place of the cable anchor assembly depicted on the standard sheet. Is this substitution compliant with the plan's component requirements?
In Plan 511-1A, the contractor replaces the V-mesh end strips with flat wire mesh panels at the enclosure ends. Is this substitution consistent with the component depicted on the plan?
For Plan 202-1 mailbox support, the contractor installs a round steel post instead of the breakaway wooden post shown in the standard. Is this component substitution compliant?
A Plan 203-2A fill section is constructed using rock riprap on the scarified surface in place of the prepared soil layer required by the section drawing. Is this compliant with the section detail?
